tweet.text:
Mexican forces used Black Hawk helicopters firing miniguns yesterday during the operation to arrest the high-level cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores (“El Chapo Isidro”)

The cartel leader was an FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive and was arrested  Guasave, Sinaloa.

Mexican special forces secured him along with his second-in-command Serafín and his financial operator José N.

The operation triggered cartel counter-actions including roadblocks, vehicle burnings and clashes across parts of Sinaloa.

The three were quickly extracted by air to Mexico City for judicial processing. 

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was born in 1982 and rose through the ranks of the Beltrán Leyva cartel as a young man later led the independent Cartel de Guasave / Los Mazatlecos. 

That group focused on drug trafficking (including fentanyl and meth) from northern Sinaloa into the U.S., with presence in Sonora, Durango, and Nayarit, and was aligned at times with Sinaloa Cartel factions such as “Los Mayos.” 

The FBI added him to its Ten Most Wanted list in February 2025 with a $5 million reward.
